title: Streamlining financial regulation while safeguarding stability
summary: BIS General Manager Pablo Hernández de Cos delivered a speech on March 4, 2026, examining the post-GFC regulatory reforms 20 years after the Great Financial Crisis, discussing how to evaluate whether reforms achieved their resilience objectives and how to streamline frameworks while maintaining financial stability.
key_points: Post-GFC reforms have markedly increased banking system resilience: CET1 ratios stand at 14.3% vs less than 10% in 2011; equity-to-assets ratio increased from 3.5% to 6.1%
Liquidity buffers have strengthened significantly: high-quality liquid assets increased 55% from 2012 to 2025 (now 21% of total); stable funding share increased ~40% to 56% of total exposures
Approximately 50 major regulatory reforms were introduced globally post-GFC, with Basel III implementation still ongoing

The speaker outlined three key conditions for regulatory reviews: (1) start with open mind and be agnostic about outcomes, (2) conduct holistic reviews covering the whole financial system including NBFIs, (3) recognize financial stability as a global public good requiring cross-border cooperation

The speech flags that post-crisis reforms focused mainly on banking sector while NBFI regulation was strengthened much less, raising concerns about insufficient prudential controls for shifted risk exposures
Basel Framework sets a common minimum global baseline that jurisdictions can exceed, allowing proportionality elements for internationally active banks
why_it_matters: This speech provides the BIS perspective on regulatory evaluation and streamlining 20 years after GFC reforms. For market participants, it signals ongoing assessment of whether regulatory frameworks can be simplified without compromising the resilience gains achieved since 2008. The focus on NBFI risks and cross-sectoral interactions suggests future regulatory attention may shift toward non-bank financial intermediaries.
macro_context: The speech contextualizes post-GFC reforms as enabling the financial system to weather successive shocks including COVID-19, Russia-Ukraine war economic reverberations, and 2023 banking turmoil. The macro context emphasizes that enhanced banking resilience is a significant success of international regulatory cooperation.
market_structure_context: The speech directly addresses market structure through discussion of banking sector capital and liquidity requirements (CET1 ratios, equity-to-assets ratios, HQLA holdings, stable funding shares), the Basel Framework's role as a minimum global baseline, and the need to holistically regulate both banks and NBFIs to prevent risk migration and regulatory arbitrage. The speech argues post-GFC reforms focused mainly on banking while NBFI regulation was strengthened much less, potentially leaving insufficient prudential controls for shifted risk exposures.
